executiveSummary: GM0225's 2025 code, Druten name, Gelderland province, Gelderland-Zuid safety-region assignment, 19,748-person control total, 26 neighbourhoods, five BAG places and seven settlement labels are coherent. All ten canonical exercises execute deterministically at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 across power, water, drainage, gas, telecom, mobility, facilities and supply; exact-zero input, finite bounds, reconciliation, monotone event-attributable burden, causal-ledger closure, standing-water recovery guards and layer invariance pass. The current route rule is also materially improved: Druten's three NWB border links are used only for Mobility and road-logistics/Supply, never as power, water, drainage, gas, telecom or facility topology. Release nevertheless remains correction-required. The river preset holds generic normalized inundation stress at 3.072542 through T+72, grows affected population-equivalent from 12,565 at T+24 to 13,290 at T+72 and accumulates 721,335.974 local pre-network person-hours without a selected Waal boundary condition, Zuidelijke Waaldijk defence state, breach/overtopping path, connected footprint, arrival or recession. Waal-side Deest ranks 23rd and Bedrijventerrein Deest last, while unrelated pluvial, coastal, heat and wildfire layers share one complete neighbourhood order. A controlled source inside official BRT loofbos in Verspreide huizen Horssen ranks its containing neighbourhood only 17th. Public Rivierenland rain, defence and water-register data, 117 local water objects, external acute care, provider areas and current observations are useful context but do not provide complete operational topology, capacity, state or restoration. Those unavailable or security-sensitive facts must remain Unknown or transparently synthetic.

evidenceSources.title: Omgevingsvisie Druten 2025-2040 and current municipal preparedness/energy pages
evidenceSources.edition: Adopted 2 October 2025; published 23 December 2025; current preparedness and electricity pages accessed September 2026
supports: The official vision places Druten, Afferden and Deest along or directly behind the Waalbandijk; Deest is an industrial dike village with industry partly outside the dike. It identifies the Drutense Waarden, Drutense Bos and Laakbos and a summer foot/bicycle ferry Druten-Dodewaard.

The municipality targets climate resilience by 2050 for heat, drought, water nuisance and weather; by 2035 it seeks a green-blue rural structure and water storage. It calls for protecting sewer/electric cabinets from peak rain/seepage, cables and pipes from heat and emergency accessibility under all conditions.

The current page https://www.druten.nl/projecten/wat-te-doen-bij-noodsituaties confirms a 24/7 regional crisis team but says Druten and the safety region are still researching where and how emergency support points will be established. It is preparedness context, not an activated site/capacity register.

The current page https://www.druten.nl/projecten-energie/elektriciteitsvoorziening says Liander is expanding substations because the grid is overloaded and that voltage problems or outages may occur, while explicitly saying whether and when is unknown. This is planning context, not outage telemetry.

The legal announcement is also available as HTML/XML/ODT/PDF at https://zoek.officielebekendmakingen.nl/gmb-2025-568579.html. No event API, reuse licence or fixed operational refresh cadence is stated; these documents must not become observations or a T+72 forecast.

evidenceSources.title: Zuidelijke Waaldijk Oost project and official defence/water GIS downloads
evidenceSources.edition: Current project information and established water/defence map services accessed September 2026
supports: The Zuidelijke Waaldijk Oost trajectory is 35.5 km from Weurt to Dreumel and runs along Deest and Druten; space is constrained where the dike passes homes and industry in Deest. The authority says parts do not meet statutory norms but explicitly says this does not mean the dike is unsafe now.

The exploration runs through 2028, followed by plan development in 2029-2030 and a stated total duration of roughly eight to nine years. It is project/assessment context, not a breach, overtopping or incident-time condition.

The maps page https://www.waterschaprivierenland.nl/kaarten exposes viewer, WMS/WFS/ArcGIS and GeoPackage/GDB/DWG downloads for established watercourses, water defences, level areas and wastewater infrastructure. Relevant REST roots include https://portal.wsrl.nl/kaarten/rest/services/Waterveiligheid/Legger_en_Werkingsgebieden_Waterkeringen_Vastgesteld/MapServer and https://portal.wsrl.nl/kaarten/rest/services/Watersysteem/Legger_en_Werkingsgebieden_Wateren_Vastgesteld/MapServer.

The public services use RD New geometry and are integration-ready as legal/register context, but the page/service metadata does not state a standard reuse licence, contractual cadence or live performance SLA. Legal geometry and project status do not establish defence strength, control state, hydraulic connectivity, capacity or future performance.

evidenceSources.title: Klimaatatlas Rivierenland and HWH IMWA/DAMO managed-water registers
evidenceSources.edition: Klimaatatlas web map modified 7 August 2026; local rain layers identify a 2018 2D model; HWH deployment snapshot 2 September 2026
supports: The public ArcGIS web map https://www.arcgis.com/sharing/rest/content/items/3269a57f3d0647198556b32050401169/data?f=json exposes Waterdiepte bui 60 mm/1uur stedelijk gebied (2D 2018), 60 mm/1 h flow paths, NBW 2004/2014 rural inundation, level/catchment/watercourse layers and national flood, heat, drought and nature-fire layers.

The 60 mm/1 h depth service is at https://portal.wsrl.nl/kaarten/rest/services/Grondwater/WaterOpMaaiveldInundatie/MapServer and advertises EPSG:28992 plus JSON/GeoJSON/PBF-capable dynamic queries. The web-map item is public but has blank licence and terms fields and no contractual cadence; its regional landing page explicitly says the maps identify potential vulnerability and are not suitable for concrete measures without local data.

The generated full-boundary intersection contains 117 HWH objects: six sewer pumps, RWZI Druten, seven surface-water pumps and 103 weirs. Example named sewer-pump register capacities are Afferden 82, Deest 123, Horssen 89, Druten Kalverstraat 210, Druten West 292 and Puiflijk 316, but units/operating envelopes are not normalized in the app.

HWH IMWA is a national weekly OGC API and HWH DAMO is contributor-dependent, both CC BY-SA 4.0; direct endpoints are https://api.pdok.nl/hwh/waterschappen-kunstwerken-imwa/ogc/v2 and https://api.pdok.nl/hwh/waterschappen-waterketen-damo/ogc/v1. Coverage is explicitly partial and a record, status or capacity field does not prove connectivity, operation, backup or restoration.

Simulation role is official static scenario/register context and coverage validation first. No Atlas or register layer may be treated as current observation, scenario-aligned forecast, physical topology or causal service availability without authority validation, complete metadata and a NoData contract.

evidenceSources.title: Rampbestrijdingsplan Dijkdoorbraak en Overstroming and Zorgrisicoprofiel 2024
evidenceSources.edition: Flood-response plan current PDF; health-risk profile adopted 25 April 2024
supports: The regional flood-response plan distinguishes multi-day high-water-wave warning from faster failure mechanisms: Waal/Nederrijn-Lek waves may give roughly five to ten days, while piping failure may give about half a day.

It treats evacuation as extra-municipal and potentially longer than two days, and says non-inundated as well as inundated areas can lose vital infrastructure. It requires consideration of preventive gas, power and drinking-water shutdown, roads, fuel, supermarkets, buses, shelters, reverse lanes and coordination with Liander, Vitens, Gasunie, telecom and ProRail.

The Zorg­risicoprofiel at https://www.vrgz.nl/media/3889/zorgrisicoprofiel-2024-ghor-gelderland-zuid-spreads.pdf prioritizes high-river flooding, contaminated drinking water, electricity failure, ICT/telecom failure and a toxic shipping incident as care-chain stressors.

These fixed planning PDFs have no machine event API, stated open-data licence or live refresh cadence. Their correct simulation role is mechanism, decision and response-context validation, not neighbourhood probability, current activation, operator state or restoration promise.

supports: BRT feature b3d0ccee-1bdb-52ee-856a-c0c702c3c0a0 is official loofbos. Its centroid [5.598234538258141, 51.86579630971909] is inside the full GM0225 boundary and BU02250601 Verspreide huizen Horssen; 353 BRT forest polygon parts intersect the municipality in the audit query.

BRT Top10NL OGC is nationwide/current topographic context under CC BY 4.0; feature-level origin/registration dates vary and the collection snapshot is not current fuel, moisture, accessibility, ignition, perimeter or suppression state.

KNMI FDSN is an automatically updated event-origin API under default CC BY 4.0. Zero GM0225 earthquake origins in the 365-day deployment catalogue is no matched origin, not zero probability, shaking or damage; a selected event still requires a ground-motion/site-response surface.

Rijkswaterstaat Waterinfo generally supplies ten-minute point observations under CC0 and is non-mission-critical. Zero assigned GM0225 water-level/discharge points means no municipal point coverage, never zero Waal level, discharge, flood exposure or safety. RVO's definitive 2025 BRP WMS/WFS/Atom is annual/CC0 land-use context, not current crop/fuel condition or food stock.

KNMI radar observations and other current observations must retain observation/issue/valid time and licence. They can validate scenario context only when temporally aligned and can never be copied forward as a synthetic T+72 forecast.

findings.evidence: Under river flood, seven service availabilities are exactly unchanged from T+24 to T+72 and facilities falls from 0.494598 to 0.308822 while every recovery factor stays zero. VRGZ describes evacuation, preventive utility shutdown, road/fuel/bus/shelter coordination and multi-operator decisions, but no such selected decision/action, resource or completion state drives the model.

findings.summary: Storm, coastal, heat/drought, winter, cyber, earthquake and compound values are bounded exercises rather than calibrated Druten observations or forecasts.
findings.evidence: At T+24 storm gives severity 0.116360 and supply availability 0.484120; coastal gives zero direct water/affected but wind 18.231876 m/s and telecom 0.884788; heat gives 24.117229 C, drought stress 0.536023 and water 0.581444; winter gives gust 26.883263 m/s, -9.482235 C, snow 4.539428, ice 0.759053 and supply 0.309442; cyber gives stress 0.497898 and telecom 0.351557. Earthquake peaks between checkpoints at T+2.25 with severity 0.017919/PGA 0.005734 g and zero affected at required checkpoints. No named weather replay/forecast, cyber target/architecture, seismic event/grid or local fragility validates these values.

residualLimitations: This is an audit of a deterministic first-72-hour planning exercise, not a warning, probability estimate, hydraulic assessment, evacuation order, outage statement, clinical-capacity statement or operator restoration commitment.

No expert-selected Waal hydrograph, gauge/datum, Zuidelijke Waaldijk state, breach/overtopping path, inner-/outer-dike mask, connected footprint, arrival/recession, dewatering, verified depth unit or NoData mask drives GM0225; normalized inundation stress is not metres.

The WSRL 60 mm/1 h 2D-2018 rain layer and other Atlas products are official static regional scenario/context with an explicit not-for-concrete-measures warning, blank licence/terms and no complete cadence/cell/NoData contract; they are not observations or T+72 forecasts.

The generalized 65-position CBS outline is suitable for overview rendering, not detailed river, dike, rain, forest, road, ferry, building or asset intersection; analytics must use the 1,231-position official geometry.

CBS small-area values can be rounded or suppressed; the -8 population source-sum difference is publication semantics, null fields remain Unknown and registered residents do not equal incident-time presence.
HWH and WSRL registers do not establish complete connected catchments, compatible capacity units, current pump/weir/RWZI/defence state, control logic, pressure, contamination, backup or restoration.

No complete public causal Liander feeder/switching, Vitens pipe/pressure/quality, gas pressure-district, municipal sewer, telecom backhaul or facility topology is consumed; unavailable or security-sensitive detail remains Unknown.

NWB roads, NDW messages, GTFS stops and the summer foot/bicycle ferry do not establish incident-time operation, bridge/ferry state, evacuation throughput, emergency access or repair access. Current/no-match traffic cannot be projected to T+72.

No internal RIVM acute-care point exists in the register; straight-line distance to Tiel is not ambulance travel time, reachability, acceptance, staffing, occupancy, diversion or generator/fuel endurance.

Government and education locations are not confirmed crisis centres, emergency support points, shelters, care sites or distribution points. The municipality says support-point roles/locations remain under study.

Provider territories and the one NBNL postcode sample identify responsibility/planning context only, not complete municipal coverage, topology, current load, outage, switching, reserve or restoration. Missing sewer/media provider matches remain NoData.

Zero local Waterinfo, PM2.5, NDW and seismic records is a time/point/coverage result, not zero water, smoke, disruption, shaking or risk. RDI antenna sites do not establish radio coverage, traffic, backhaul, power/backup or availability.

BRT forest and BRP parcels are static land-use/eligibility context, not current fuel, moisture, ignition, perimeter, suppression or smoke exposure; the controlled ignition is a reproducible model test, not a real event.

Cyber lacks a named target, architecture, attack path and operator state; earthquake lacks a selected event, site-response/ground-motion surface and asset fragility; coastal zero water is only the canonical preset's narrow direct component.

Affected population is a post-network people-equivalent threshold metric while deprived person-hours is a cumulative local pre-network matched-baseline pressure proxy. Neither is identified customers, casualties, displacement, welfare loss or economic damage; six-hour checkpoints can miss rapid transitions.
Exact service percentages, local ranks and recovery paths remain synthetic exercise output until each hazard/service has a versioned calibration, uncertainty, action and evidence-state contract.
